jobs.title: Staff Product Manager
jobs.description:
What we're building

Jiga is on a mission to help engineers build physical products faster.

The problem: engineers designing physical products waste weeks chasing quotes, vetting suppliers, and managing procurement instead of actually engineering. Jiga fixes this by connecting engineers directly with vetted manufacturers (CNC, sheet metal, injection molding, 3D printing). Think "npm install for mechanical engineers" - get the parts you need without the admin nightmare.

We're a small, fully-funded, cashflow-positive team serving enterprise customers like NASA, Google, Tesla, and Apple.

The role

We're looking for an execution-focused, zero-fluff Staff Product Manager. Someone who can take ownership and drive product initiatives with a high degree of autonomy. You'll be making calls on what we build and why, translating messy customer and operational problems into simple solutions, and making sure they're executed well, monitored, and improved over time.

How we actually work

We’re a small remote team made up of the best of the best. Our team members are distributed around the globe, with product and engineering talent across Europe, Israel, and the US. You’ll also work with teammates in Asia. Most of our work happens async, which is the secret sauce of our success.

High trust, low bullshit: We don't count hours or peek over your shoulder on Slack. We trust you to get your work done and tell us when something's wrong. You'll have real ownership over what you build, no process theater, no busy-work meetings.

Question everything: See something that doesn't make sense? Say it. Have a better way to do something? Just do it. We actually mean it when we say we want people to challenge the status quo and improve things. Our internal motto is “Don’t drink the kool-aid.”

No busy work, no fluff: We keep processes lightweight and practical. If something helps us work better or solve a real problem, we do it. If it creates work without adding value, we question it.

Actually friendly, not corporate friendly: We play games online every week (current favorite: Make it Meme). Once a year we fly everyone somewhere beautiful for our offsite. We genuinely like hanging out together, which turns out to be way better than forced "team building exercises."

What we value in product and engineering:

Simple > Complicated. Simple code, simple architecture. Simple solutions are better than complex ones.

Ship it, then improve it. Perfection is the enemy of done. Launch now, iterate forever.

Product > Engineering. Every line of code should make our users' lives better. We're not here to show off our algorithmic prowess - we're here to solve real business problems.

Financials

Jiga is fully funded, cashflow positive, with growing revenue MoM. We're completely transparent about our runway and finances - ask us anything.

What you'll actually do

  • Talk to customers and suppliers, and work closely with internal users to understand their workflows and pain points (not just read reports about them).

  • Go deep into a complex problem and come back with a simple solution.

  • Analyze and monitor product usage data yourself to inform decisions and measure results.

  • Define what we build next and why, then write specs engineers can actually execute on.

  • Work closely with engineering and design to take solutions through delivery, follow up after launch, and improve what isn’t working.

  • Collaborate with sales, CS, and operations to understand business needs and improve internal processes.

  • Take ownership and move things forward independently without exhausting approval loops.

  • Clearly communicate what we’re not focusing on and why.

  • Use AI throughout all of the above to move faster, go deeper, and get more done.

What we're looking for

Must have:

  • You've built meaningful products that people use and that drive business results.

  • 5+ years in product, including experience owning complex initiatives independently.

  • Startup experience (<50 people). You know what “do everything” means.

  • Actually hands-on: you've done user research, written specs, built prototypes, and prioritized backlogs yourself. Recently. Not five years ago before you “moved to strategy.”

  • Comfortable with data, dashboards, and product analytics. You ask the right questions, find the answers yourself, and question what the numbers are telling you.

  • You know what moves the needle, focus on that, and separate real problems from noise.

  • You go deep with engineers, communicate clearly in writing, keep stakeholders aligned, and ask users questions that uncover real needs.

  • You're willing and able to get into operational details, work with internal teams, and improve how things get done.

  • You use AI hands-on in your daily work and have experience building AI-powered features that deliver real value within users’ workflows.

  • Strong UI/UX instincts. You have opinions about the details.

  • At least 4 hours of overlap with GMT+3 working hours.

Nice to have:

  • A background in industrial design, mechanical engineering, or supply chain.

  • Hands-on experience as a software engineer, data analyst, or UI/UX designer.

  • B2B experience in collaboration tools, quoting, supply chain, manufacturing, CAD, logistics, or marketplaces.

You'll love it here if

  • You're energized by ambiguity, not paralyzed by it. "Figure it out" sounds like freedom, not abandonment.

  • You have strong opinions loosely held. You're decisive but update quickly when you're wrong.

  • You're low-ego, high-output. You do the grunt work, not just the strategy decks.

  • You see gaps and fill them without being asked.

  • You say what you think. No corporate speak, no hedging, no "let's circle back."

  • "If I can solve this without pulling in a dev, I'll just do it" is how you operate.

  • You're obsessively curious about manufacturing and how things get made.

This might not be for you if

  • You need meetings to get things moving.

  • You prefer clear requirements handed to you.

  • You like building consensus before making any decision.

  • "Move fast and break things" gives you anxiety.

  • You want to focus on "strategy" and have someone else handle the details.

  • You can’t operate without a clear process and hierarchy.

What we offer

  • A small team where you matter: We never compromise on people. That means you are part of the best team in the world.

  • Zero bureaucracy: We hate process theatre as much as you do.

  • Real ownership and responsibility: Make decisions, ship solutions, own the outcomes.

  • Complete flexibility: Work from anywhere, set your own hours, take time off when you need it (parents especially welcome).

  • Genuinely high trust: We trust you to do great work and be honest when things go sideways.

  • A team that actually likes each other: International, diverse, genuinely friendly people who enjoy working together.

  • Generous stock options: Meaningful equity in the company you’re helping build.

  • Self-development budget for books, courses, conferences, whatever helps you grow.

  • Annual offsites in beautiful places.

  • Fast-paced environment with tons of creative freedom.

  • Hard, interesting problems with a team that's positioned to win big.

How to apply

Tell us about a product decision you made that was controversial at the time but turned out right. And one that turned out wrong.

Product Owner – Inspection Instruments for Infrastructure (Hardware & Software) (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
Intro

We are looking for a motivated and technically driven Product Owner Infrastructure to join our product management team at Screening Eagle Technologies and take ownership of our Infrastructure inspection portfolio –measurement instruments (sensors, electronics) combined with embedded app software. You own the product across its full lifecycle: from market and customer requirements, through the phased development process, to launch, pricing and phase-out

You will play a key role in ensuring technical excellence, assessing the feasibility of new features, aligning stakeholders, and supporting sales activities through customer visits, exhibitions and technical training


What will you do

  • Managing the full product lifecycle (PLC) of hardware products: concept, development phases and gate reviews, launch, phase-in / phase-out of product generations and accessories
  • Collecting Voice of Customer and market input and turning it into market requirements, business cases and a product roadmap
  • Working with R&D (hardware, firmware, software), operations, supply chain and service on feasibility, cost targets, certification and production readiness
  • Translating business goals and user needs into clear technical requirements, epics, user stories and acceptance criteria
  • Acting as the primary technical point of contact for hardware and software development teams, clarifying specifications and supporting daily development activities
  • Assessing architectural impact and ensuring the technical feasibility of new features before sprint planning
  • Maintaining and prioritising the backlog with the development teams; writing user stories and acceptance criteria for product and app features
  • Communicating technical constraints, risks, and project progress effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Supporting sales teams during customer visits, exhibitions, and industry events
  • Preparing and delivering technical training materials, seminars and webinars to support customers and internal teams
  • Collaborating with cross-functional teams to ensure product development aligns with business objectives and technical requirements


What do we expect

  • At least 3 years of experience as a Product Owner or Technical Product Manager of physical / hardware products, ideally combined with embedded or app software
  • Experience with a phase-gate product development process and with product phase-in / phase-out
  • Strong technical background, ideally with hands-on experience or solid foundational knowledge in optics development; experience with NDT or construction / civil engineering is a strong plus
  • Proven ability to translate complex business requirements into clear technical specifications for development teams
  • Familiarity with Agile methodologies
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a data-driven approach to decision-making
  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with cross-functional and international teams
  • Willingness to travel
  • Ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced and international environment
  • Fluency in English and German, both written and spoken


Our offer

  • Competitive remuneration package
  • Team building events and company activities 
  • Opportunities for professional development 
  • Free car parking
For this position we only consider direct applications via our platform

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager - Bookkeeping
jobs.description:
Are you looking to have an impact on the daily life of millions of entrepreneurs in France (and tomorrow in Europe)?

Are you looking for a work environment that values trust, proactivity, and autonomy?

Are our Product Principles aligned with your vision?

Then Pennylane is the right place for you !

 

Our vision

We aim to become the most beloved financial Operating System of French SMEs and Accounting Firms (and soon, European ones).

We help entrepreneurs rid themselves of time-consuming tasks related to accounting and finance while providing them with access to key financial information to assist in making the best decisions for their business.

 

About us

Pennylane is one of the fastest growing Fintechs in France (and soon to be in Europe!)

 

In almost 7 years of existence, we’ve managed to :

💻 Make ourselves known as a groundbreaking accounting and financial software for small businesses and their accountants

💰 Raise a total of €225 millions, including from Sequoia, the famous fund from the Silicon Valley who invested early in companies like Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal and much more...

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Grow from 7 cofounders to 1300+ happy Pennylaners : we’re now recognized as one of the greatest places to work in France (and also remotely), with a 4.6/5 rating on Glassdoor.

🌍 Build an international environment with more than 25 nationalities, with a strong remote-friendly culture, where 30% of the employees are already working from all parts of Europe

🤝 Earn the trust of thousands of customers and accounting firms and obtain outstanding ratings

🚀 Already more than 1M+ small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and over 4,500 accounting firms use Pennylane in France!

WHY this position is of utmost importance to reach our mission

Autopilot is Pennylane’s AI add-on for accounting firms, designed to automate bookkeeping and move accountants from execution to supervision—with a clear ambition: a 1-click VAT return.

The challenge is no longer only to build a powerful product, but to activate it at scale, prove its value and turn adoption into revenue.

As the first PM of the new Bookkeeping / Autopilot Growth squad, you will play a central role in making that happen. You will help hundreds of thousands of companies adopt Autopilot, connect firms to the value it already delivers and shape Pennylane’s AI monetization strategy.

HOW you will contribute to the company as a Product Manager

As a Senior Product Manager, you will join a 100+ person Product organization, working with 300+ engineers to make Autopilot the default way firms run their bookkeeping.

You will:

  • Understand what drives adoption. Talk to firm owners and accountants, analyse product data with SQL, Amplitude and Metabase, and identify where firms hesitate to activate Autopilot.

  • Turn insights into measurable growth. Define clear hypotheses, metrics and stop criteria, then run B2B experiments through holdouts, cohort analysis and staged rollouts.

  • Own the growth strategy. Set your OKRs, shape the roadmap and focus the squad on the initiatives that drive activation, trust, usage and revenue.

  • Build with a cross-functional squad. Partner closely with a Product Designer, Engineering Manager and product-focused engineers, starting with MVPs and iterating based on what you learn.

  • Work across the ecosystem. Collaborate with the squads building Bookkeeping and Autopilot, as well as Data, Product Marketing, Pricing, Sales, Customer Success and Account Management.

  • Scale adoption beyond the product. Design in-product and lifecycle experiences that help firms self-serve, while providing commercial teams with the signals they need to support adoption.

  • Build for France and Germany from day one. Design configurable solutions rather than simple translations, and work with the German team to make what works in France scalable internationally.

  • Help define a new way of building product. Work agentic-first, design for supervision and stay relentlessly user-obsessed—using AI tools and agents every day to explore data, prototype and move faster.

WHAT you can expect from your life at Pennylane

Within one month

  • You'll learn everything about our company, our teams, and our vision during the first onboarding week

  • You'll familiarize yourself with the product, the accounting industry and the accountant channel (you will have access to a lot of documentation and will attend trainings organized by your peers)

  • You'll understand how Autopilot works: what it automates, how confident it is, and where it still needs a human

  • You'll have mapped the Autopilot adoption funnel, at company and firm level: eligible, enabled, expanded, paying

Within 3 months

  • You'll have set the adoption baseline and targets with your manager

  • You'll have shipped and read your first experiments on activation, hand in hand with your Product Designer and Engineers

  • You'll have impacted positively at least one OKR

  • You will have set up your continuous discovery routine with firms and be ready to build your roadmap

Within 6 months

  • You'll be autonomous at defining your OKRs and your roadmap

  • You'll have shipped at least one step change in how firms activate Autopilot

  • You'll have made the time Autopilot saves visible to firm owners

  • You'll have prepared the switch to paid with Pricing, Product Marketing and Sales

  • You'll have equipped Account Managers and CSMs with an adoption playbook they actually use

  • You'll share your learnings and playbooks with the other Autopilot squads and with Germany

What do we do to make your work life easier

 

🏢 You'll be able to work remotely from anywhere in Europe, as long as your contract allows you to;

📈 You'll get company shares to enjoy a piece of the success story you're building with us;

🏡 You’ll have a budget to turn your home into a more comfortable workspace, as well as a monthly allowance to work from a coworking space whenever you feel like it;

⛹️Through our partner Gymlib, you’ll have access to 8000 fitness spaces in Europe and more than 300 activities related to wellness;

🇬🇧 You’ll have access to Busuu to perfect your English or your French;

💻 You’ll get the latest Apple equipment;

🎉 You’ll be part of a vibrant social community : we do lots of sports together (Foot, running, climbing...), we love to hang out and have a drink together (thursday afterwork drinks on our rooftop is a usual thing. Twice-a-year we do company seminars, last time we went on a trip to the French Alps and it was fabulous !).

 

And.. If you're based in 🇫🇷 :

 

🏢 You’ll be able to work fully from your home or any co-working space in France, or from our wonderful office in the center of Paris

🏝You’ll get 10 additional days off (to the 25 standard ones) to rest and do what you love each year

🍜 You’ll have lunch credits (Swile card) to buy your favorite food every day

🏥 You’ll have a great healthcare cover (Alan Blue) to take care of yourself and your family

 

We're working on providing those last advantages to our people based outside of France as well, but it can be quite more complex depending on different countries.

What does the recruitment process look like?

  • You will first have a general chat with Charlène, Talent Acquisition Manager (45 min)

  • You'll then have a discussion with one member of our Product team to assess the fit and the Product culture (45 min)

  • You'll then pass a live case study on an Autopilot adoption problem with 2 Product Managers from our team (1h15)

  • You'll have a final round with Tancrède (our CPO) and a Group PM or a Head of Product (60 min)

We make sure we move fast; you can expect the recruitment process with us to last between 15 and 25 days in total.

Language

For this specific role, a full fluent level in French 🇫🇷 is required.

What you’ll bring

  • Proven experience driving growth, adoption or monetization, ideally in B2B SaaS or a scaled B2C product, with measurable results;

  • Strong data fluency and hands-on analytical skills: you can go from SQL query to dashboard to actionable decision, using Amplitude or equivalent tools—even when the data is imperfect;

  • Rigour in experimentation: you know when sample sizes are too small for A/B testing and can design robust holdouts, cohorts and staged rollouts instead;

  • A strong understanding of AI-powered products: you can assess automation quality across confidence, accuracy, coverage and evaluation—and know what it takes to build user trust;

  • Excellent product sense and user research skills: you can uncover what makes professional users comfortable delegating critical work to a machine;

  • Strong cross-functional leadership: you influence and align multiple squads and commercial teams without relying on formal authority;

  • Clear, structured communication skills, with fluency in French and professional proficiency in English;

  • Previous Product Management experience in a scale-up or large technology company.

Experience in accounting is not required, but curiosity for the domain and comfort with complexity are essential. Experience with pricing and packaging, free-to-paid transitions, paid add-ons, lifecycle/CRM or sales-assisted PLG would be a strong plus.

🇫🇷 Données personnelles

Pennylane traite vos données pour gérer votre candidature et évaluer votre adéquation au poste. Si votre candidature n’aboutit pas, vos données peuvent être conservées 2 ans à compter de notre dernier échange ou de la clôture du recrutement afin de constituer & gérer un vivier de candidats. Vous pouvez vous opposer à tout moment et demander la suppression de vos données en écrivant à :
Notre data policy

🇬🇧 Personal Data

Pennylane processes your data to manage your application and assess your suitability for the position. If your application is unsuccessful, your data may be retained for 2 years from our last exchange or the closing of the recruitment process, in order to build and manage a candidate pool. You may object at any time and request the deletion of your data by writing to Learn more

🇩🇪 Personenbezogene Daten

Pennylane verarbeitet Ihre Daten, um Ihre Bewerbung zu bearbeiten und Ihre Eignung für die Stelle zu beurteilen. Sollte Ihre Bewerbung nicht erfolgreich sein, können Ihre Daten bis zu 2 Jahre ab unserem letzten Austausch oder dem Abschluss des Rekrutierungsverfahrens gespeichert werden, um einen Kandidatenpool aufzubauen und zu verwalten. Sie können jederzeit Widerspruch einlegen und die Löschung Ihrer Daten beantragen, indem Sie an Mehr erfahren

🇪🇸 Datos personales

Pennylane trata sus datos para gestionar su candidatura y evaluar su idoneidad para el puesto. En caso de que su candidatura no sea seleccionada, sus datos podrán conservarse hasta 2 años a partir de nuestro último contacto o de la finalización del proceso de selección, con el fin de constituir y gestionar una reserva de candidatos. Puede oponerse en cualquier momento y solicitar la eliminación de sus datos escribiendo a Más información

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
The challenge
An entrepreneur chasing an unpaid invoice in Lagos. A shop owner confirming a shipment in Guangzhou. A consultant navigating a bank's phone menu in London. For a growing share of Talk360's 6 million+ users, a call is how they get paid, keep a client or close a deal.

These business customers choose us because we're cheaper than carrier and roaming rates, reach mobile, landline and company numbers, need no contract, and use one balance for every country. Today we serve them with a consumer app. Tomorrow we want to be the obvious way small businesses call the world.

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own and scale the Calling for Work product proposition from 1 to 100. There's no mature roadmap to inherit: you'll write it, test it with customers and scale what works, with our Product & Tech team, to deliver a step change in segment growth.

What you’ll do

  • Own the product proposition: Set the vision, strategy, roadmap and targets for Calling for Work, and be responsible for its user growth and retention.

  • Shape the business proposition: Define what Talk360's business offer is and how it's priced, together with our commercial teams.

  • Learn from customers continuously: Use interviews, surveys, support tickets and app store reviews to turn pains into a ranked opportunity roadmap.

  • Experiment fast: Ship small bets, A/B test the journeys that matter, observe real world behaviour and turn results into roadmap decisions.

  • Lead delivery: Work in an agile Product & Tech team; keep scope tight, priorities clear and releases flowing.

  • AI-native execution: Use AI across discovery, specs, analysis and prototyping, and help shape how the team builds with AI.

  • Partner across the business: Work with Revenue, Marketing, Support and Data on go-to-market, acquisition, retention and the metrics that show we're winning.


The Team

You'll join a lean Product & Engineering team where product, design, mobile, web, backend, VoIP and QA work closely together. No silos, no layers: turn a customer insight on Monday into a live experiment by Friday.


What you’ll bring

  • 5+ years in product management, including owning a product line or new proposition end to end.

  • A track record of scaling a product from early traction, with commercial results to show.

  • Hands-on experience with B2B, SMB or prosumer products; telecoms is a plus.

  • Strong discovery skills: customer interviews, research synthesis and jobs-to-be-done thinking.

  • Experimentation fluency: A/B testing, product analytics (Mixpanel or similar) and data analysis and data-driven decision making.

  • Experience optimising MAU, ARPU, LTV, retention and conversion, with the business acumen to make strategic and tactical calls.

  • Experience leading agile, cross-functional mobile product teams, with the technical depth to discuss trade-offs with engineers.

  • Active, daily use of AI across your product workflow: research, analysis, specs and prototyping.


Who you are

  • Growth mindset: You're energised by building a playbook that doesn't exist yet.

  • Ambitious and pragmatic: You aim for 100 but ship the smallest thing that proves the next step.

  • Owner: You act without waiting for permission and own outcomes, not output.

  • Customer-obsessed: You'd rather talk to five customers than debate one assumption.

  • Clear communicator: You align engineers, leadership and partners around one simple story.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity: You make good calls on imperfect data and kill what isn't working, even your own ideas.

  • You're based in or moving to The Netherlands and can be in our office three days a week.


Recruitment process

  1. First call: A short intro call with our recruiter.

  2. Hiring manager interview: A deep dive into your experience with our Head of Product.

  3. Case study: Present a practical Calling for Work challenge to the team at our office.

  4. Meet the CEO.

  5. Reference check

  6. Offer

What You Get  

Competitive compensation  

  • 77,000 - 90,000 euros per year all-in gross

Learning and growth  

  • €1,500 annual personal development budget, plus access to company-wide training sessions to keep learning and evolving.  

Time to recharge  

  • 25 vacation days   

  • Option to swap two public holidays per year for days that better reflect your culture or beliefs   

  • Recharge Fridays, unlocked when team targets are met (we’ll tell you more during the interview)   

Work from anywhere  

  • As a global and diverse team, we encourage you to work from another city or country for up to 2 weeks per year, gain fresh perspectives and spark new ideas.  

A team you’ll actually want to be part of  

  • Weekly team lunch every Thursday   

  • Regular team moments and outings   

  • An international and diverse team, with colleagues from the Netherlands, South Africa, Nigeria, Suriname, Turkey, Egypt, Kenya, Ukraine and beyond   

Set up for success  

  • Company laptop and all the tools you need to do your best work   

  • Monthly phone allowance and commuting allowance   

An environment to grow and make impact  

  • A collaborative environment where you can learn from others, take ownership, and contribute to a meaningful mission.  

About Talk360  

Talk360 has grown into a global communications platform connecting more than 6 million people worldwide. We've successfully spun off our payments business into NjiaPay, stepped into the gap left by Skype, and built a profitable, sustainable business. 

We're now expanding beyond our own consumer app through our SDK, enabling partners to integrate Talk360's calling infrastructure directly into their own products. 

Our ambition is simple: To become the world's most trusted way to call any phone number.

 

Here’s what our users say:  

“I like Talk360 because it saves me a lot of money. I used to call from Zimbabwe for 15 rands a minute. Talk360 came to the rescue. Now I can call my mother for hours.” — Google Play, South Africa ★★★★★  

“Talk360 is a simple and reliable app for cheap international calls. It works even if the receiver has no internet, offers good call quality, and has transparent pricing.” — Google Play, United States ★★★★★  

“It is a flawless experience with no hustles at all and the tariffs are more than just fair.” — Trustpilot, United Kingdom ★★★★★

Bouw mee aan het digitale fundament van de volgende generatie Mijn Independer. Wil jij richting geven aan een platform waarop miljoenen veilige en betrouwbare klantinteracties plaatsvinden? Lees dan verder.

Wat ga je doen als Product Owner Digital Customer Platform?
Als Product Owner Digital Customer Platform ben je verantwoordelijk voor één van de belangrijkste platformteams binnen Independer. Je geeft richting aan het digitale fundament van Mijn Independer 2.0 en vertaalt complexe technische vraagstukken naar een heldere productvisie, duidelijke prioriteiten en concrete resultaten. Met jouw werk maak je veilige, betrouwbare en schaalbare klantinteracties mogelijk en creëer je de basis voor personalisatie, AI-oplossingen en toekomstige digitale dienstverlening. Zonder deze rol ontbreekt de technische basis waarop nieuwe klantfunctionaliteiten gebouwd worden.

Concreet ga jij aan de slag met:
Je werkt op het snijvlak van productontwikkeling, architectuur, security, data en engineering. Daarbij houd jij je onder andere bezig met:

  • Het bepalen en uitdragen van de productvisie voor het Digital Customer Platform.

  • Het prioriteren van de backlog in samenwerking met architecten, tech leads en andere stakeholders.

  • Het aansturen van ontwikkelingen rondom digitale identiteit, autorisaties, klantidentificatie, accountbeheer en personalisatie.

  • Het realiseren van de integratie van nieuwe platformdiensten, waaronder CIAM-oplossingen, en het bewaken van technische kwaliteit, schaalbaarheid, stabiliteit en ontwikkelsnelheid.

  • Het vertalen van strategische ambities naar een uitvoerbare roadmap en het vinden van de juiste balans tussen innovatie, technische schuld en operationele betrouwbaarheid.

Team
Dit doe je uiteraard niet alleen, maar samen met een groep gezellige en gedreven collega's. Je werkt intensief samen met teams binnen Data & AI, Mijn Independer Frontend, Customer Experience, Architectuur en Security. Samen bouwen jullie aan de technische basis van Mijn Independer en ontwikkelen jullie oplossingen voor digitale identiteit, authenticatie, autorisaties, klantidentificatie, accountkoppelingen, personalisatie en AI-gedreven dienstverlening. Daarnaast werkt het team continu aan het verbeteren van stabiliteit, performance, developer experience en het verminderen van technische schuld.

Wat wij bieden

  • Salaris tot max 6.300 euro o.b.v. 40 uur, vakantiegeld en een jaarlijkse bonus;

  • 30 vakantiedagen en een premievrij pensioen;

  • Reiskostenvergoeding en een thuiswerk- en internetvergoeding;

  • De mogelijkheid om voor 50% vanuit huis te werken;

  • In de winter in de zon werken? Ga een aantal weken op workation;

  • Veel ruimte om te groeien en ontwikkelen d.m.v. ons brede opleidingsaanbod;

  • Leuke events, borrels en sportactiviteiten;

  • Dagelijks een uitgebreide en gezonde lunch;

  • Een fijn kantoor met gratis parkeergelegenheid en station Hilversum op loopafstand;

  • En natuurlijk een bedrijf vol enthousiaste collega's!

Wat wij zoeken
Je voelt je thuis in een complexe platformomgeving en weet technologie, business en klantwaarde met elkaar te verbinden. Daarnaast breng je het volgende mee:

  • Minimaal 4 jaar ervaring als Product Owner of Product Manager.

  • Ervaring met digitale platformen, SaaS-producten of klantplatformen en affiniteit met software-architectuur en technische vraagstukken.

  • Ervaring met stakeholdermanagement binnen een complexe organisatie en een analytische, datagedreven manier van werken.

  • Je begrijpt hoe moderne platformen, API's, identity-oplossingen en cloudomgevingen werken, zonder zelf developer te hoeven zijn.

  • Je durft keuzes te maken, prioriteiten te stellen en strategische ambities te vertalen naar een heldere roadmap.

jobs.title: Digital CS Program Manager
jobs.description:
About us

Rentman is a B2B SaaS scale-up building a smart, powerful operations management platform to support event and media production teams. Our users plan everything from small shoots to massive festivals in 70+ countries, and they all rely on Rentman to keep their gear, people, and timing perfectly in sync. We’re based in Utrecht (NL) with a second office in Toronto (CA), and our 120+ team members work in a culture that’s open, flat, and inclusive, where curiosity drives us, ownership matters, and everyone has the freedom to challenge ideas and make an impact. Check out our public roadmap to see what’s coming next!

Mission of this role

Thousands of customers, most of our customer base, work with Rentman without a dedicated Customer Success Manager. They sign up, set up Rentman and get to work, but not all of them get the most out of what they pay for, and today we mostly help them when they reach out to us. We want to change that. Your job is to make sure every one of them gets the most out of what they pay for, starting with new customers in their first months. Instead of adding CSMs at the same rate as we grow, we’re building a system of signals, plays and AI agents that helps these customers adopt Rentman, stay and grow with us. However, a human touch always stays: our pooled CSMs step in at the moments where a person makes the difference.

This is a new role and a new function, and you start as a team of one. You’ll build Digital CS from the start, with support from Data, Ops and AI engineering and a direct report to our Head of CX. There’s room to shape how AI agents are used in Customer Success, and a growth path towards CS or Revenue Operations.

What you'll do

  • Explore product usage, engagement, billing and support data in BigQuery to find which behaviour predicts adoption, churn or contraction. Turn those signals into trigger rules: what counts, from which threshold, at what moment and for which customer group. You build the data models behind these signals yourself, with our Data team reviewing your work.

  • Build automated plays across email and in-app messaging in tools like HubSpot and Chameleon, starting with new customers who haven’t adopted the product yet. You also automate the processes around your plays yourself, including AI steps. Every play defines when a customer goes to a pooled CSM, for example when there’s a cancellation signal or no response to the automated steps.

  • Every play runs against a control group. Ship a small version first, measure whether the effect is real or noise, improve what works and stop what doesn’t.

  • Write and maintain the customer communication for your plays across email, in-app and agent instructions, in language that fits our brand.

  • Shape agent specs and prompts that AI engineering builds from: tasks, rules, examples and when to hand over to a person. Define test cases and quality criteria, and check the agent’s work every week the way you would a team member’s.

  • Work with the onboarding squad, Content & Community, Product Marketing and RevOps so plays fit their designs and don’t clash with launches or product tours, and help decide which CS tools we build on.

Your first year

  • First 3 months: you find the first signals and set baselines together with our Data team.

  • After 4 months: your first plays for new customers are live, each running against a control group.

  • By the end of your first year: around 8 plays are live, at least 5 of them with a proven effect, and you’ve run a first pilot with an AI agent.

What we are looking for

  • 3+ years driving scaled adoption or retention for a large customer base, for example in scaled or digital Customer Success, CS or Revenue Operations, lifecycle or CRM marketing, or growth, at a SaaS or subscription business.

  • Proven experience turning product usage data into health scores, signals or lifecycle triggers.

  • A track record of one-to-many programs with results you can show in numbers, including how you knew the change came from the program and not something else.

  • No need to wait for an admin: you build workflows and sequences yourself in tools like HubSpot, or Chameleon.

  • Solid SQL skills: you write and read it independently.

Nice to haves

  • You’ve built a CS program or function from scratch (0 to 1), not only taken one over.

  • Hands-on work with agent specs or AI-supported workflows in a CS or support setting, and using AI daily for writing, analysis and testing while knowing its limits: wrong answers, privacy, and when a person has to step in.

  • A background in the live event, AV or equipment rental industry.

  • Experience in Git and pull requests

What you’ll get

  • A results-based bonus based on company performance (up to a full 13th month's salary)

  • 25 vacation days to recharge

  • Earn an extra day of PTO for each year at Rentman, from your second anniversary up to five years.

  • Flexible WFH policy & work from anywhere for 4 weeks a year

  • An OV Business card if you live more than 10km from the office

  • An ambitious, inclusive, and diverse international team

  • A flexible, energizing workplace with free lunches, office perks (PS5, ping pong, D&D), legendary karaoke nights, and regular team activities

  • An amazing office in the heart of Utrecht, in the historic Drift 17

  • A steep learning curve feels daunting: We move fast and use cutting-edge AI; you need to be an aggressive self-learner who can master new domains in days, not months.

    • Our culture (read this carefully)

    Our culture is defined by three things:

You’ll know the people you work with, you’ll be able to walk over to anyone to ask a question or test an idea, and you’ll be part of the day-to-day energy of building together:  from whiteboard discussions to shared lunches, dogs in the office, and moments to pause and reset.

    We hire smart, ambitious people who think like owners, value intellectual honesty, and are motivated by impact rather than comfort. If you enjoy challenge, responsibility, and building something meaningful with others, you’ll likely thrive here.

    If you’re looking for predictability, narrow scopes, or a guaranteed 9-to-5, this likely won’t be the right fit - and that’s okay. We’d rather be honest upfront.

jobs.title: Associate Product Manager (f/m/d)
Associate Product Manager (f/m/d)
Senior Product Manager, Financial Statement Suite
jobs.description:
Before a company publishes its annual report, finance teams have to turn financial data into a complete set of statements and disclosures. Balances need to be mapped, figures carried forward and updated, and supporting information brought together into a draft. Auditors then check that the notes match the primary statements, this year reconciles with last year, and every total adds up. Preparing and reviewing those statements takes days of detailed work, and errors can carry through into a published report.

Today, audit teams rely on Financial Statement Suite (FSS) to read statements, run checks, and show reviewers what it found and where, so they can make the call and stand behind it. The opportunity goes beyond reconciliation: helping auditors and financial professionals review drafts, connect figures to supporting evidence, and manage changes through to sign-off.

You'll own what FSS becomes across preparation and review cycles. You'll decide what sits on the teams roadmap and define strategy for this high opportunity area working with engineering, design, audit experts and the firms who use FSS every day.

About DataSnipper

The hardest AI problems aren't about getting an answer fast. They're about getting one people can trust.

We believe trust is essential to how society works. Every day, we rely on information that's been independently verified, from financial statements to the products we buy, to the sustainability claims companies make. Behind that trust are audit and finance professionals who examine evidence, verify information and hold organizations accountable.

At DataSnipper, we build AI solutions that empower those professionals. By making evidence easier to trace and verify, we help them focus on the judgment and expertise that make their work so important.

For our product and engineering team, this is where things get exciting. In audit, a plausible answer isn't good enough. Every output has to be explainable and traceable back to its source. We've just launched a brand new agentic platform, Alwin by DataSnipper. AI agents running in the cloud across hundreds of documents at once, reasoning across PDF, Word and Excel, with a full audit trail behind every step. There are lots of greenfield problems ahead, and real room to shape what we build and how we build it.

And we build at scale. More than 600,000 professionals across 3,000+ organizations in 175 countries rely on DataSnipper, including Fortune 500 companies, government agencies and all Big Four audit firms. In 2025 alone, the DataSnipper platform delivered more than $1.4 billion in productivity savings to is customers. Backed by a $100 million Series B led by Index Ventures, at a $1 billion valuation, and as proud members of 1% for the Planet, we care about how we grow, not just how fast.

If you want to build AI that professionals trust with work that really matters, this is your chance to help shape the future of audit and finance and do the best work of your career along the way.

 

What impact you will have

  • Own the end-to-end strategy and decisions for our financial statements product, with clear domain ownership

  • Lead product direction in a key area with direct and clear business impact

  • Reimagine how auditors and financial professionals work, making their workflows more defensible

Why it's an exciting challenge

  • Reviewers are sceptical, and they should be. A finding they can't trace is a finding they check again by hand.

  • Statements differ by country, by standard and by firm. FSS has to be right on all of them, not just the ones in front of you this week.

  • Firms use FSS when the stakes are highest. Every change has to make their next busy season better, not riskier.

  • Everyone has a request: firms, sales, partners and engineering. You'll decide which ones the evidence supports, and say no to the rest.

What you'll own

  • The full FS experience: how a team moves through a draft, from the first finding to sign-off

  • Trust in every check: each finding shows what it compared, where the figures came from, and who reviewed it

  • Quality: what "ready to ship" means for each check, and how the team knows a change helps without breaking something else

  • Where FSS goes next: which statement types, standards and markets come first, and why

     

What you'll do

  • Set the plan and make trade-offs explicit, including new checks versus improving the ones customers already rely on

  • Spend time with auditors: watch real reviews, see where they double-check by hand, and turn that into product decisions

  • Work with engineering and audit experts on sets of real statements that every change has to pass

  • Use product data to decide: which findings reviewers accept, reject or ignore, and why

  • Build on Alwin's shared platform capabilities, and raise dependencies with other teams early

  • Help sales and customer success decide which customers and statements FSS is ready for

  • Write clearly: decisions, specs, and requirements so the team can drive forward with clarity and speed

What you'll bring

Must-have:

  • Product management experience on B2B software where getting it right matters: audit, accounting, tax, legal, compliance or financial services

  • A strong business acumen and focus on business impact

  • Experience shipping AI, machine learning or document-processing features, and making their output something people can check

  • Comfort with data: you can read an error analysis, query your own numbers and spot a sample that isn't representative

  • A record of prioritising for a large user base with demanding customers and competing stakeholders both internal and external

  • Enough technical depth to make trade-offs with engineers on accuracy, data and architecture

Strong-to-have:

  • An audit or accounting background, or deep knowledge of financial reporting (IFRS, US GAAP, UK GAAP)

  • Creative mindset thinking beyond how problems are solved today to reimagine a future approach that drive productivity

  • Experience in agentic products, workflows and systems

 

What We Offer

  • Be part of one of the fastest-growing, profitable unicorn scale-ups in the Netherlands with a global impact.

  • Equity (Stock Appreciation Rights) to share in the company’s success and growth.

  • Pension plan with a 6% contribution on top of your base salary.

  • 28 vacation days per year (full-time) to support your work-life balance.

  • Hybrid work model with at least 3 days onsite in our dynamic Amsterdam office.

  • Daily, freshly prepared lunches by our in-house chef to keep you energised.

  • NS business card for easy commuting to the office.

  • A structured onboarding programme designed to set you up for success, including dedicated time to learn our product and customers before you hit the ground running.

  • Access to continuous learning and development initiatives to grow your skills.

  • Engage with a vibrant international team spread across seven global offices.

  • Company-wide events like DataSnipper GO, where global teams come together.

  • Access to OpenUp, a mental health and wellness platform supporting your wellbeing.

 

Recruitment steps

What matters to us is what you can bring to the role, the team, and DataSnipper. 🚀

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager, Strategic Initiatives
jobs.description:
Who is Sonar?

Sonar enables organizations to ship agentic code with confidence. Code creation is abundant, but confidence is scarce. Our core platform, SonarQube, verifies over 750 billion lines of code every day, delivering agentic verification and governance for all code. Trusted by more than 7 million developers and 75% of the Fortune 100, including teams at Nvidia, ServiceNow, Booking.com, Goldman Sachs, AstraZeneca, and Ford Motor Company, Sonar enables organizations to reduce outages, improve security, and lower the cost and risk of agentic software development.

Founded in Geneva and now headquartered in Austin, Texas, Sonar has a global team working across offices and hubs, including Silicon Valley, London, Bochum, Barcelona, Singapore, Tokyo, and the Washington, D.C. area. At Sonar, we’re enabling enterprises to build agentic software factories that can move quickly while maintaining the control, consistency and evidence required to ship with confidence. 


Position description

Sonar is becoming an AI-first company. Strategy Enablement turns Sonar's strategic ideas into real, lasting results: company-critical initiatives, business transformations, acquisition integrations and new market expansion. As Sr. Project Manager, Strategic Initiatives, you will lead some of these initiatives from fuzzy intent to measurable outcome with pace and focus, as a trusted thought partner to leadership. Everything we do ultimately serves our internal and external customers, and you will keep them at the center of the solutions you design. You will reinvent both how projects are run and what they deliver: you use AI agents every day in your own work, and you design solutions AI-first, ambitious yet practical. Your first focus will be the AI transformation of our Go-To-Market organization, with our Business Technology team (including SALT, its AI team) and the Data & Insights team. Over time, you will lead initiatives across the company, in domains you may not know yet.

What you will do

  • Frame ambiguous strategic intents into clear problems, objectives and business cases, starting from the impact on our customers and the business.

  • Bring the customer voice into every initiative: use customer feedback and data to shape solutions, and make sure internal changes improve how customers buy, use and renew with Sonar.

  • Ground decisions in data: establish baselines, size opportunities, define success metrics up front and measure impact after go-live.

  • Lead complex, cross-functional initiatives end to end, driving pace and keeping the focus on customer and business outcomes.

  • Re-plan quickly when priorities or context change, and recommend stopping work that no longer pays off.

  • Redesign processes AI-first, from the outcome back: decide what AI agents do, where humans and AI work together and where human judgment stays essential, with guardrails proportional to business risk.

  • Build working prototypes (skills, agents, lightweight apps, automations) to test ideas early with users, then partner with Business Technology to industrialize what works.

  • Use AI agents systematically in your own business analysis and project management work, and share reusable skills and workflows to raise the AI bar around you.

  • Bridge leadership and operational teams: engage stakeholders early, manage competing priorities and keep sponsors and teams aligned.

  • Stay agile and pragmatic: run initiatives with simple, effective tools and communication rather than heavy process and admin, pick the approach that drives the behaviors and actions needed, re-plan quickly when context changes, and recommend stopping work that no longer pays off.

  • Master business analysis and project management foundations, and apply them pragmatically: just enough process, simple tools and clear communication, never process for its own sake.

  • Own change management as part of delivery (communication, training, champions, reinforcement) until new ways of working stick, with particular care for the human side of AI-driven change.

Experience and qualifications

The ideal candidate will:

  • Have 10+ years of experience leading complex, cross-functional, international transformation or strategic initiatives, ideally combining strategy or transformation consulting with in-house experience in a fast-growing tech or SaaS company.

  • Bring a proven track record of measurable outcomes (revenue, cost, efficiency, adoption, customer experience), not just projects delivered.

  • Have a strong customer mindset: see internal work as a way to serve customers, and use that lens to set priorities.

  • Use AI agents and assistants (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) hands-on every day, with concrete examples of skills, agents or workflows they have built.

  • Have designed or delivered AI-enabled processes, with a pragmatic view of AI's value, limits and risks.

  • Be strongly data-driven: analyze business data themselves (spreadsheets, SQL or BI tools, AI-assisted analysis) to build business cases and track results.

  • Demonstrate strong change management, stakeholder management and communication skills, having led people through significant change and influenced executives and operational teams alike.

  • Master business analysis and project management foundations, and apply them flexibly rather than by the book.

  • Thrive in ambiguity: decide with partial information and adapt the plan without losing sight of the goal.

  • Show strong curiosity and learn new domains quickly. Go-To-Market experience is a plus.

  • Be fluent in English, written and spoken. French is a plus.

In-office culture

We're intentional about this. We believe the best teams are built in the room together. Three anchor days — Mondays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays — create the collaboration rhythm that makes a hub office worth having. 

Candidates need to be genuinely based in the location the role is posted  — if that's not where you are today, we're happy to support relocation for the right person.

 

We value diversity, equity, and inclusion

At Sonar, we believe that our diversity is our strength. We are a global company that values and respects different backgrounds, perspectives, and cultures. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive work environment where everyone feels valued and empowered to contribute their best. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and welcome all qualified applicants, regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

If you need any accommodation, please reach out to us at All offers of employment at Sonar are contingent upon the results of a comprehensive background check and reference verification conducted before the start date. 

Applications that are submitted through agencies or third party recruiters will not be considered.

About the role

We're looking for a proactive, data-driven Associate Product Manager to join our UK Loans product team. You'll play an important role in shaping the customer experience after they take out a loan: from how we engage with customers and manage payments, to how we support those who experience financial difficulty.

APMs at Zable take ownership of their product changes, working closely with teams across Engineering, Credit, Finance and Operations to solve problems and take the business to the next level.

What you’ll work on

What we're looking for

jobs.description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The team

Mistral is building a sovereign AI cloud for Europe. Our customers in finance, healthcare, and the public sector run frontier models on European-jurisdiction infrastructure, and the Cloud Platform team builds the systems that make that possible, from compute orchestration and Kubernetes to bare metal, storage, and networking.

European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on and shape the team building it.

The Role

As a Storage Product Manager on the Cloud team, you will own the strategy and roadmap for Mistral's storage product portfolio. You have a deep understanding of the storage stack from block storage, distributed filesystems, object storage, and the evolving storage technology that accelerate AI/ML and HPC workloads. You understand what is slowing down the infrastructure teams building on Mistral Cloud — translating those insights into products that are flexible, easy to build on, and performant at scale.

You will work closely with engineering and cross-functional teams to build new products and enhance existing offerings, ensuring alignment with technological advancements, customer expectations, and market trends. This is a highly critical role with significant influence over the future of AI compute and storage products.

What You’ll Do

  • Product strategy: Define and execute the product vision for Mistral's storage offerings — including distributed filesystem, block, and object storage to keep pace with the needs of AI training and inference at scale.

  • Cross-functional leadership: Partner with Cloud Software Engineering, and SRE to define technical specifications, execution timelines, and the performance, reliability, scalability, and cost targets the different storage products must hit.

  • Data strategy and architecture: Drive the data lifecycle, tiering, durability, and failure-domain strategy in close partnership with engineering.

  • Roadmap ownership: Own and prioritize the storage product roadmap, balancing customer requests, technical feasibility, and business impact.

  • Customer discovery: Build deep relationships with the infrastructure teams building on Mistral Cloud, understand their storage needs and pain points, and act as their voice inside the company.

  • Market Analysis: Research trends, opportunities, and challenges in the storage domain, and use these insights to guide product development and positioning.

  • Technical translation: Distill complex technical tradeoffs into clear, compelling narratives and decision documents for company leadership.

  • Performance monitoring: Track and analyze product performance metrics and use data-driven insights to guide product enhancements and future direction.

What We’re Looking For

  • 8+ years of experience in product management, with a strong focus on storage and cloud infrastructure, particularly in high-performance or AI-driven environments

  • Strong understanding of storage technologies, including file system, block and object storage.

  • Solid technical foundation and cloud-infrastructure knowledge. You’re comfortable reasoning about API semantics, control-plane vs data-plane behavior, system events and lifecycle, multi-tenant operational realities. You can engage with engineering teams as a peer, not as a translator. You can challenge an engineering tradeoff, not just relay one.

  • Strong analytical instincts with the ability to use data to inform and defend multi-year infrastructure decisions.

  • Ability to align and inspire cross-functional teams without direct authority, and to communicate credibly with executives, engineers, and customers.

  • Low ego, high bias for action, and comfort in ambiguity — equally at home crafting a strategy narrative and diving into metrics, a UX detail, or a customer escalation.

Bonus

  • You can reason about cloud storage economics, and how tiering across hot, warm, and cold tiers affects cost

  • You've designed, or worked closely on, backup, replication, or disaster recovery products

  • You're comfortable discussing storage performance characteristics: throughput, latency, IOPS, and how they map to real workloads

About Zable

Zable (formerly Lendable) is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money.

Zable was founded on the belief that smarter technology is the solution to lower cost, more transparent consumer finance. Our proprietary foundation models analyse thousands of data points in seconds, drawing a more complete picture of individual financial behaviour. This means we can make better risk decisions, widening access and lowering prices.

The Zable credit card harnesses this technology to deliver better borrowing for three million people. Through our superapp, Zable connects this card to a single platform which makes it effortless to manage credit, get a loan, refinance existing borrowing, switch utilities, get a mobile plan and save more.

Zable is now the number one issuer of new credit cards and personal loans in the UK, but we’ve barely got started. Next, we’re taking our approach to some of the biggest markets in the world - the US and Mexico - where hundreds of millions of people are underserved by outdated bank processes.

Join us if you want to

  • Take ownership across a broad remit - you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Zable from day one

  • Work in small teams of exceptional people - who are relentlessly resourceful to solve problems and find smarter solutions than the status quo

  • Build the best technology in-house - using new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

 

About the role

Every email and notification we send is part of how customers experience Zable, and a 5.0★ Trustpilot rating across more than 100,000 reviews sets a high bar for it: communication has to be clear, timely and honest. As our Senior Product Manager for CRM & Growth, you'll own the products and systems that shape how customers hear from us across their lifecycle, from first interaction through to retention and reactivation.

Product here isn't backlog grooming. The trade-offs are commercial as much as they are user-facing: engagement, retention, conversion, cost to serve and customer experience all pull against each other, and you'll make the calls. There will always be more good ideas than capacity, so sharp prioritisation is central to the job. The role also has a real technical edge. Messaging reliability, deliverability and platform integrations are part of what you'll own, so you'll need to be comfortable going deep with engineers. Teams here are small relative to the size of the book we run, so you'll carry more scope and ownership than the same title would at a larger, more layered company.

What you'll be doing

  • Owning the roadmap and outcomes for our CRM and lifecycle product: onboarding, engagement, retention and reactivation

  • Prioritising a pipeline of competing opportunities across CRM, growth, deliverability and platform work, weighing expected impact, effort and risk, and being clear about what we won't do

  • Taking products and channel improvements from problem definition through to launch and iteration, owning both the product and technical decisions alongside Engineering

  • Defining the metrics that matter and making the commercial trade-offs between growth, retention, cost and customer experience, and making sure performance is measurable end to end, from tracking and data flows through to dashboards the wider business can trust

  • Running an experimentation programme: writing clear hypotheses, designing A/B tests, and using SQL and our data to measure true incremental impact

  • Treating email deliverability and messaging reliability as product concerns, working with Engineering on infrastructure, platform integrations and cost efficiency

  • Shaping requirements with Engineering, Design, Marketing, Risk and Compliance so that what we ship is effective and meets the standards expected of a regulated lender

  • Holding a high bar for what customers receive: clear, honest content, well-tested design, and rigorous checks before and after launch.

What we're looking for

Essential

  • 5+ years in product management, with substantial experience in CRM, lifecycle, messaging or growth for a consumer product at meaningful scale

  • Strong product management fundamentals: you've taken a product or channel from problem definition through launch and iteration, and owned both the product and the technical sides of delivery

  • Excellent prioritisation: a clear, defensible way of ranking competing opportunities by expected impact, effort and risk, the confidence to say no, and the ability to explain trade-offs to stakeholders

  • A track record of owning measurable outcomes in engagement, retention or revenue, not just shipping features

  • Strong SQL and analytical skills, and experience designing and interpreting A/B tests, with the habit of measuring impact rigorously rather than relying on vanity metrics

  • Enough technical depth to work credibly with engineers on messaging infrastructure, deliverability and platform integrations, and clear communication across technical and commercial audiences

Nice to have

  • Experience in financial services or another regulated industry

  • Experience launching a new channel or capability end to end, such as push notifications across mobile and web

  • Experience building experimentation or measurement tooling, including getting CRM and messaging data into a BI environment for analysis

  • Experience mentoring other product managers or CRM specialists


Interview process

  1. A quick chat with someone from our Talent team to see if the role is a good match

  2. A 15-minute cognitive assessment.

  3. A practical exercise or case study interview with the Hiring Manager

  4. A culture-add interview to assess how you'd thrive within our team and organisation

  • Build the best technology in-house - using new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

 

About the role

We're building a larger, dedicated Platform team at Lendable, increasing our investment in the infrastructure that enables our products and engineering teams to scale.

We're hiring a Technical Product Manager to sit within Engineering and connect platform technology, reliability and commercial value. You'll own what we prioritise and why, giving engineers the business context they need while helping Product and leadership understand the impact and opportunities that Platform enables.

This is a hands-on technical IC role, where you'll stay close to engineering through writing code, reviewing PRs and contributing to architecture discussions.

Working closely with the Platform Engineering Manager and Tech Lead, you'll help shape the Platform roadmap, connect technical investment to measurable business outcomes, and build the foundations that allow Lendable to move faster and scale with confidence.

What you'll be doing

Own platform stability

  • Own platform stability as a primary accountability - SLA/SLO metrics, incident rates, release quality.

  • Hold release gating authority: block features from production that don't meet testing standards or introduce unacceptable regression risk.

  • Enforce CI/CD standards centrally so pods don't fragment into one-off solutions.

  • Track and report stability metrics alongside commercial outcomes - stability is the foundation that makes the rest possible.

Be commercially accountable

  • Own the business case for platform investment and answer "why are we spending six engineers on this for three months?" in terms leadership understands.

  • Track platform impact in business terms: developer velocity, incident cost, time-to-market, reliability, capacity - e.g. "CXO rollout removes a 3-second API fan-out, reducing session abandonment" or "we can now handle 20k simultaneous logins".

  • Input into headcount and investment decisions for the platform team.

Own the platform roadmap

  • Own the platform backlog, prioritised by business value and sequenced to unblock the highest-value product teams first - not driven by technical debt or engineer preference alone.

  • Make trade-offs explicit: "if we do X now, we defer Y by Z weeks - here's what that means for products depending on us".

  • Ensure every initiative has a defined success metric that non-engineers can track.

Be the stakeholder interface

  • Act as the single point of contact for Pod Leads: business requirements coming from pods and engineering/developer requirements flowing to pods; prioritise both in service of platform stability.

  • Make platform work visible to leadership - regular forums with product MDs and PMs to capture upcoming dependencies before they become blockers; represent platform work in leadership reviews; translate technical milestones into business milestones.

  • Drive cross-team collaboration and buy-in with other PMs; engage architecture in technical design.

  • Escalate when product teams make requests that would create unsustainable platform load or technical debt.

Contribute as an engineer

  • Write code, review PR's, and participate in architecture design as a core part of the role - not a side project.

  • Bring a strong technical voice to roadmap decisions without owning final architecture calls (that's Architecture and Tech Leads).

What we're looking for

Essential

  • Deep, hands-on engineering background - this role must be staffed by someone who has shipped production systems, not someone who has only managed backlogs.

  • Strong commercial instinct: can build a business case, speak to P&L impact, and hold a line on ROI.

  • Exceptional stakeholder management across product, engineering, and finance without direct line authority over all of them.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity - platform value is often indirect and long-horizon.

  • Track record of contributing as an IC while operating at a senior, cross-team level.

  • Proactive, low-ego, and clear communicator - able to hold a line with leadership and pod leads alike.

Nice to have

  • Experience in platform, infrastructure, or developer tooling contexts.

  • Familiarity with SLA/SLO frameworks and incident management at scale.

  • Experience enforcing CI/CD standards across multiple teams or pods.

  • Prior work making "invisible" infrastructure legible to non-technical leadership.

Our tech stack

Platform & backend: Kotlin, AWS, Postgres, RabbitMQ, Docker, Kubernetes.

Gateway & clients: Node GraphQL gateway, React Native / TypeScript mobile app, Relay.

Tooling & observability: GitHub, GitHub Actions, Jira, Confluence, Datadog, Sentry, Grafana.

Interview process

  • Quick call with the Talent Team (30 minutes)

  • Hiring manager interview (30 minutes)

  • Technical and Product interview (90 minutes)

  • Culture-add interview (60 minutes)

Life at Zable

  • The opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies

  • Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites

  • Socials & connection: opportunities and events to come together, socialise, and get to know each other beyond the office walls

  • Health coverage: support for your physical and mental wellbeing, including private health cover

  • Retirement & savings: long-term financial wellbeing through retirement savings plans

  • Employee referral programme: earn a competitive bonus when you refer successful new team members

  • Office meals & snacks: enjoy a fully stocked kitchen, plus complimentary lunches prepared by in-house chefs on in-office days at select locations

  • Sustainable commuting: cycle-to-work and electric vehicle salary sacrifice schemes available in select locations

Please note: The availability and details of specific benefits vary by location and role. For more information, please speak to your Talent Partner.

jobs.description:
Über EVEREST

EVEREST ist Ideengeber und Projektentwickler für digitale Tools, die Gründer*innen und Kleinunternehmer*innen Zugang zu wirtschaftlichem Know-how, Kapital und Ressourcen ermöglichen. Wir entwickeln Empowerment-Plattformen von der Konzeption bis zum Betrieb – z.B. die kostenlose bundesweite Gründerplattform oder das digitale Beratungsprogramm InStart für Soloselbstständige und Kleinunternehmen in der Krise in Hamburg. Deren Nutzer*innen haben Zugang zu ständig aktualisiertem Wissen, können ihre eigenen unternehmerischen Pläne umsetzen, wichtige Kontakte knüpfen und als Community voneinander profitieren.

Zur Verstärkung unseres Teams am Standort Hamburg-Altstadt suchen wir dich in Vollzeit oder Teilzeit für eine befristete Position als:

Senior Product Owner (m/w/d) – Digitale Startup-Plattform

Das erwartet dich

Eine gute digitale Anwendung macht komplizierte Dinge einfach. Genau daran arbeitest du bei uns.

Wir entwickeln ein neues digitales Plattformprojekt rund um die Themen Gründung und Startups. Dahinter stehen verschiedene Teilprojekte, komplexe fachliche Anforderungen und viele Ideen, die sinnvoll miteinander verbunden werden müssen.

Als Senior Product Owner sorgst du dafür, dass aus diesen Ideen ein durchdachtes, technisch realisierbares und vor allem nutzerfreundliches Produkt entsteht.

Du arbeitest eng mit der Geschäftsführung, Projektleitung und unserem Entwicklungsteam zusammen. Dabei erwarten wir, dass du Entscheidungen fachlich hinterfragst, Abhängigkeiten erkennst und eigene Lösungsvorschläge einbringst.


Deine Aufgaben

  • Produktentwicklung steuern: Du behältst die verschiedenen Teilprojekte im Blick, erkennst Abhängigkeiten und sorgst dafür, dass Funktionen in einer sinnvollen Reihenfolge entwickelt werden.

  • Entscheidungen fundiert vorbereiten: Du prüfst Ideen und Anforderungen auf Nutzen, Logik und technische Machbarkeit. Wenn ein geplanter Entwicklungsschritt noch nicht sinnvoll ist, erklärst du, warum das so ist, und zeigst Alternativen auf.

  • Komplexität für Nutzer*innen reduzieren: Du übersetzt komplexes Expertenwissen rund um Gründungsprozesse in einfache, intuitive digitale Anwendungen. Dabei berücksichtigst du die unterschiedlichen Bedürfnisse und Herausforderungen von Gründerinnen – von der ersten Geschäftsidee über die Gründung bis hin zum Wachstum. Dein Anspruch: Nutzerinnen finden in jeder Phase die passende Unterstützung, ohne selbst Expert*innen sein zu müssen.

  • Nutzererlebnisse konzipieren: Du entwickelst mit Figma eigenständig User Flows, Wireframes und interaktive Prototypen, überprüfst Konzepte anhand von Nutzerfeedback und optimierst sie gemeinsam mit dem Team.

  • Entwicklung konkret voranbringen: Du übersetzt Anforderungen in verständliche User Stories und Entwicklungstickets, priorisierst das Product Backlog und klärst fachliche Fragen direkt mit dem Entwicklungsteam.

  • Roadmap und Qualität im Blick behalten: Gemeinsam mit Geschäftsführung und Projektleitung planst du realistische Entwicklungsschritte, begleitest neue Funktionen bis zum Go-live und nutzt Feedback und KPIs für die weitere Optimierung.

Das bringst du mit

Du hast bereits digitale Produkte entwickelt und weißt aus Erfahrung, dass eine gute Idee allein noch kein gutes Produkt ergibt.

  • Erfahrung im Produktmanagement: Du bringst mehrjährige Erfahrung als Product Owner oder Product Manager mit und hast digitale Produkte bereits eigenverantwortlich von der Konzeption bis zur Umsetzung begleitet.

  • Technisches Verständnis: Du kannst Anforderungen mit Entwickler*innen auf Augenhöhe besprechen, technische Abhängigkeiten nachvollziehen und daraus praktikable Lösungen ableiten. Erfahrung mit Low-Code-Plattformen ist ein Plus.

  • Sehr gute Figma-Kenntnisse: Du kannst selbstständig interaktive Prototypen entwickeln und hast ein fundiertes Verständnis von UX/UI und nutzerzentrierter Produktentwicklung.

  • Analytisches und strukturiertes Denken: Du erkennst frühzeitig, wenn Anforderungen nicht zusammenpassen, technische Voraussetzungen fehlen oder Prioritäten angepasst werden müssen.

  • Eigenständigkeit und Kommunikationsstärke: Du vertrittst deine fachliche Einschätzung klar und nachvollziehbar und behältst bei mehreren parallelen Themen den Überblick.

  • Agile Produktentwicklung: Du bist vertraut mit Scrum, Backlog-Management und Tools wie Asana. Du kennst außerdem Möglichkeiten, KI sinnvoll in digitalen Produkten und Prozessen einzusetzen.

  • Fundiertes Startup-Verständnis: Du verstehst den Lebenszyklus eines Startups – von der ersten Idee über die Gründung und den Markteintritt bis hin zu Wachstum und Skalierung. Du weißt, dass jede Phase unterschiedliche Herausforderungen mit sich bringt, und kannst dich schnell in die jeweiligen Bedürfnisse und Fragestellungen von Gründer*innen hineindenken. Eigene Gründungserfahrung ist ein Plus, aber keine Voraussetzung.

  • Verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse und gute Englischkenntnisse

Das bieten wir dir

  • Ein Produkt mit Gestaltungsspielraum: Du bist früh in die Entwicklung eines neuen Plattformprojekts eingebunden und kannst Konzepte, Funktionen und Nutzererlebnisse aktiv mitgestalten.

  • Einfluss auf die Umsetzung: Deine fachliche Einschätzung ist ausdrücklich gefragt. Du arbeitest direkt mit Geschäftsführung, Projektleitung und Entwicklungsteam zusammen.

  • Einen Arbeitsplatz direkt in einer der schönsten Straßen der Hamburger Altstadt (Deichstraße).

  • Grandiose Kollege*innen mit einem wertschätzenden, hilfsbereiten Spirit und einem zugänglichen Management, das immer ein offenes Ohr für dich hat.

  • Eine intensive und strukturierte Einarbeitung, die dich optimal auf deinen Job bei uns vorbereitet.

  • Ein faires Gehalt zwischen 55.000 € und 65.000 € brutto jährlich bei einer Vollzeitstelle – je nach Erfahrung und Qualifikation. Bei Teilzeit wird das Gehalt anteilig entsprechend der vereinbarten Wochenstunden berechnet.

  • Teilzeit- und Homeoffice-Möglichkeiten.

  • Feedback-, Vertrauens- und Duz-Kultur.

  • Snacks und Getränke.

  • Teamevents.

Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung mit einer kurzen Info zu deinem möglichen Starttermin und deiner zeitlichen Verfügbarkeit (Wochenstunden und Tage). Bei Fragen steht dir Vanessa Klein gerne zur Verfügung.
